author: reek
body: Layout runs here too: comp-render lays the root out against the real panel rectangle from the handoff cells and returns the bounded tree, so a caller can hit-test against the same wn-bounds the pixels came from.

author: reek
body: What is deliberately NOT carried over from it: borders, shadows, gradients and accent borders. This compositor draws flat fills, every theme in the tree is flat, and a shadow is `sh-blur` filled rectangles per node per frame on a machine with no GC and no blitter.

author: reek
body: The CBF cell is 8 pixels wide at scale 1 and `gop-draw-text` advances by exactly that, so a node's capacity in characters is its inner width over 8. Text longer than that is cut rather than drawn past the node: there is no clipped text primitive on this path, so a label that overruns is drawn straight over whatever is beside it.

author: reek
body: **Every text-bearing kind is cut to its own bounds, not just inputs.** A label was not, and the first capture of the issue tracker is what that looks like: `In Progress` is 11 cells in a 72-pixel Status column and ran through the Title beside it, in a DataTable whose whole point is columns. A widget drawing outside its own rectangle also breaks the one thing the compositor promises -- that a parent's fill is covered only by its own children -- which `gop-composite-stride` asserts and could not have caught, because it measures rows against a stride rather than a node against its neighbour.

author: reek
body: The caret is placed by character index, clamped into the field, and drawn one pixel wide so an empty field still shows where typing will land.

author: reek
body: `event-dot` is the one custom tag anything in the tree uses. An unknown tag falls back to a panel fill rather than to nothing, so a widget kind this chapter has not met is visible as a block instead of silently absent.

author: reek
body: Parent first, children after, so children paint over their parent's fill. Recursion depth is the tree's depth -- chrome trees are a handful of levels.

author: val
body: The framebuffer is 32-bit XRGB with no alpha channel and no read-modify-write blend on this path, so a shadow is a hard offset rectangle painted BEFORE its box and overwritten by it, and a gradient is an exact per-row colour.

author: val
body: The framebuffer is linear and `gop-put` is one `poke-32` at `(y * stride + x) * 4`: it has no bottom and no right edge, so a y past the last scanline writes past the framebuffer and an x past the row lands on the next row. Every fill here goes through the clip. Measured 2026-08-20 at 1600x900 before the clip: 499,200 bytes written past row 899 on every paint.

author: val
body: A row no corner cuts takes one span and no reads; only cut rows pay for two boundary pixels, so a radius of 6 at scale 2 costs twenty-four blended pixels for a whole box however tall it is.

author: val
body: The whole string is measured first and returned untouched when it fits: one walk of the advance table, no allocation. Only an overflow searches, by halving, so a 32-character label that does not fit allocates 5 substrings rather than 32 on every repaint, into an arena with no collector.

author: val
body: Stores in place into the laid tree rather than rebuilding (L-ALIAS): a rebuild would have to rebuild every ancestor to repoint children. Safe only on a tree `widget-arrange` just built, whose nodes are shared with nothing.

author: val
body: The tree is laid out in LOGICAL pixels (`w / s` by `h / s`) and painted in device pixels, so the bounds on a laid tree are logical. A hit test against pointer coordinates, which are device, divides by the same scale; `comp-hit-x` and `comp-hit-y` exist so no caller invents that.

author: val
body: Text and icons are all-or-nothing against the clip: `gop-draw-text` paints a glyph as sixteen scaled rows with no row bound and `gicon-blit` knows no clip, so a line straddling the clip is dropped rather than cut.
